children: Megaspeed

said Sunday it had hired outside lawyers and launched an internal investigation after media reports raised questions about the Singapore-based cloud provider’s operations, sourcing and international supply routes following the departure of former executive
Alice Huang
The scrutiny has intensified because Huang has been tied to a

, including corporate connections to a data center serving Huawei Cloud. However, the reported business links do not establish that Huang directly supplied Huawei with Nvidia chips or that the facility received restricted Nvidia GPUs.

According to a CNBC report, Megaspeed said that Huang departed in August 2025 and said it is examining coverage about its business and supply chain while disputing that the claims are backed by checkable proof. The company also said it will decide what to share with stakeholders after it reviews the reporting.
Megaspeed’s Internal Review

The company positioned the probe as a compliance exercise, saying its controls are designed to meet export regulations and other applicable requirements in the markets where it operates. Megaspeed said it had engaged external legal counsel to conduct a "thorough internal investigation."

The business model has attracted scrutiny before, with reporting and government inquiries focusing on whether chips entering Megaspeed’s ecosystem could ultimately support users in China. Megaspeed operates in Singapore and Indonesia.
The stakes rose after former
Nvidia Corp.
chief
Jensen Huang
acknowledged infidelity following reports connecting him to Alice Huang.

Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs has also provided important context. Authorities said police and customs began investigating Megaspeed and related companies in February 2025 over suspected false declarations involving server purchases and other potential domestic offences.

Singapore said Alice Huang was not investigated for espionage. In February 2026, authorities said there was insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed the suspected declaration-related offences.
Is Alice Huang’s Departure The Key Factor?
Investors and regulators are also examining Huang’s earlier business footprint, which could shape how authorities assess potential supply-chain risks.
A private intelligence firm, Tesari, traced Huang’s indirect financial exposure to companies connected to a Chinese data center whose main customer was Huawei Cloud.
Hexi subsequently sold its Century Longteng stake in 2024. However, Tesari’s investigation said connections involving Huang’s broader business network and the data center persisted.
The research also described Huang’s husband,
Kang Wei
, as a longtime Hexi associate who later became a Century Longteng executive and attended the signing of an agreement involving Huawei.
Tesari’s vice president for national security applications,
Brian Andersen

, said the findings support a national security and technology counterproliferation review, warning that unlawful transfers of restricted computing gear to Huawei could draw export-control, conspiracy, or smuggling allegations.

Another thread runs through Huang’s earlier cloud venture, Osmanthus, which she sold to Chinese game publisher 7Road in 2019. A Singapore-based 7Road unit was later spun out as Megaspeed in 2023, and the company then grew into a major Nvidia customer.
How Executive Changes Could Reshape Nvidia’s Future
The controversy comes amid leadership upheaval at Nvidia. The company announced Thursday that Jensen Huang had
and board member, effective immediately, with CFO
Colette Kress
taking over as interim CEO.
Former Nvidia CEO Huang is also expected to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman
Brian Mast
said lawmakers had been discussing arrangements for his appearance with Nvidia, although the date and format were still being worked out.
